I've farmed these same 10.1 mu in Quzhou for 30 years, and I keep a notebook every season. My soil is alluvial loam, pH around 8.0, and I've watched the potassium decline since we stopped keeping livestock. With just my husband and me, plus our son sending money from his factory job, I have to balance every yuan. Last year wheat gave me 540 kg/mu and maize 580 kg/mu, so I'm staying close to that formula.

For winter wheat, I will use Jimai 22 — an improved variety, 13 kg seed per mu. I will rotary till after chopping the maize stalks. Base fertilizer is 50 kg of 15-15-15 compound per mu, then I topdress twice with urea: 15 kg at regreening and 10 kg at jointing. That comes to 19 kg nitrogen, 7.5 kg phosphorus, and 7.5 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate four times: overwinter, regreening, jointing, and grain filling. Two pesticide sprays — herbicide in early spring, fungicide if powdery mildew shows up. I expect 550 kg/mu if frost doesn't hit.

For summer maize, I plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid, 2 kg seed per mu, direct seeded into wheat stubble with no tillage — saves diesel and labor. I put 40 kg of 15-15-15 compound in the seed furrow, then side-dress 20 kg urea at big trumpet stage. That's 15.2 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, 6 kg potassium per mu. Three irrigations: seedling if June is dry, then tasseling, then filling. Two sprays: pre-emergence herbicide and one insecticide watch for armyworm. I'm targeting 600 kg/mu.

I learned from the China Agricultural University technicians here in Quzhou that nitrogen can be cut back without losing yield, so I dropped from 22 kg to 19 kg on wheat and held steady. I'd rather spend an extra 50 yuan on fertilizer than lose a quintal of grain — a bad harvest means borrowing money, but wasting a bit of urea is just a cost I can absorb on 10 mu. Still, I track everything: seed, fertilizer, diesel for the pump, electric bills. My total budget is about 800 yuan per mu for wheat and 750 for maize, which leaves enough for our living and some savings.
